speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing fatigue and pallor, which often points to anemia. To help narrow down the cause, can you tell me if you have noticed any black, tarry stools or visible blood in your stool recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 67-year-old male. The patient complains of a 2-month history of generalized fatigue. He mentions no specific triggers but notes that the fatigue has been progressively worsening. He denies any recent infections, significant weight loss, or night sweats.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of gastrointestinal issues, such as chronic use of NSAIDs or aspirin, or any previous diagnosis of gastric ulcers? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count

text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: Hemoglobin 8.3 g/dL (low), WBC 81,000 /mm3 (elevated), Platelets 35,600 /mm3 (low)

speaker: Doctor
text: With a white blood cell count of 81,000, this is highly suggestive of leukemia rather than simple anemia. REQUEST TEST: Peripheral Blood Smear

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Presence of immature cells with large, prominent nucleoli and pink, elongated, needle-shaped cytoplasmic inclusions.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those needle-shaped inclusions are Auer rods, which are pathognomonic for Acute Myeloid Leukemia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Myeloid Leukemia
